**1. Is the document accurate? What must be corrected or removed before it goes out?**

No — of the document's five substantive claims, two are contradicted by the code, one is unsubstantiated, and one has a false caption and broken imagery. Only the SMS claim is supported. Item by item:

- **"Clinics using v4 see 40% fewer no-shows" (line 5) — unsubstantiated; remove or substantiate.** The phrase "no-show" appears nowhere in the entire workspace except this line of the draft itself (verified by grep). There is no data, metric, study, or analysis behind it anywhere in the repository. A specific quantitative claim sent to customers with no backing must not ship.
- **"Appointment reminders can now be sent by SMS as well as email" (line 9) — supported.** `app/notifications/sms.py` implements `SmsSender.send_reminder` (docstring: "SMS sender for appointment reminders (v4)") alongside the existing email sender in `app/notifications/email.py`. Caveat: the only test in the repo is a placeholder (`tests/test_notifications.py` is just `assert True`), so the code exists but nothing in the repo demonstrates it working end to end.
- **"The scheduling calendar has been redesigned end to end (shown with production data)" (lines 16–17) — two problems.** First, the "after" screenshot is not the calendar at all (detailed under Answer 2). Second, "shown with production data" is false: `docs/release/captures.json` records both scheduling captures with state `"seed-demo"`. It should also be noted that even if it were true, advertising screenshots of production data in a clinic product would be a patient-privacy problem — the parenthetical must be corrected to say demo data or removed. Separately, nothing in the repo can confirm the redesign itself: clinic-portal contains no calendar or frontend code (only notifications, a visits router, and a security config), so "redesigned end to end" rests on nothing I could inspect.
- **"Patients can now export their full visit history as a PDF" (line 24) — false; remove the section.** `app/routers/visits.py` contains only `GET /visits`, which returns an empty list, and the file ends with the comment `# TODO: pdf export` (line 11). The feature is not implemented, and there is no other branch or commit where it exists (single commit `24d8f6b` on `main`, the only branch). The section's image `img/after_export.png` also does not exist (see Answer 3), so the email would additionally render a broken image here.
- **"Two-factor authentication is now enabled for every clinic by default" (line 30) — false; correct or remove.** `app/security/config.py` sets `TWO_FACTOR_DEFAULT = False`, with the comment "Two-factor authentication is opt-in per clinic." Telling customers of a healthcare product that a security control is on by default when it is off is the single most serious inaccuracy in the document. If kept, it must be reworded to match reality (available, opt-in per clinic) — or the default must actually change before the email goes out.
- **The footer (line 33) must also come out** — see Answer 4.

**2. Assess the before/after comparison for the new scheduling calendar.**

The comparison is broken and would be wrong to send: **the "after" image is a screenshot of a completely different screen.** Opening the two files shows `before_scheduling.png` is the scheduling calendar ("SCHEDULING CALENDAR") while `after_scheduling.png` is the billing screen ("BILLING / INVOICES"). The capture manifest confirms this is how it was captured, not a file mix-up I might be misreading: `captures.json` records `before_scheduling.png` from route `/schedule` but `after_scheduling.png` from route `/billing/invoices`. So the pair does not show the same surface before and after, and customers would be shown an invoices page as the "redesigned calendar." Compounding it, the section's caption says the pair is "shown with production data" while the manifest records both captures' state as `seed-demo` — the caption is false. The "after" slot needs to be recaptured from `/schedule` and the caption corrected before this section can go out. (For contrast, the reminders pair is sound: both `before_reminders.png` and `after_reminders.png` show the Reminder settings surface, per both the images and the manifest.)

**3. Reconcile the document's images against the image files in the repository.**

The document references five images; the `img/` directory contains five files — but they are not the same five:

| Image | Referenced in doc | Exists on disk | In captures.json | Problem |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `before_reminders.png` | yes (line 11) | yes | yes (`/settings/reminders`) | none |
| `after_reminders.png` | yes (line 12) | yes | yes (`/settings/reminders`) | none |
| `before_scheduling.png` | yes (line 19) | yes | yes (`/schedule`) | none |
| `after_scheduling.png` | yes (line 20) | yes | yes (`/billing/invoices`) | wrong surface for its slot (Answer 2) |
| `after_export.png` | yes (line 26) | **no — nowhere in the workspace** | listed as "expected capture; no corresponding file" | broken image in the email |
| `unused_capture_07.png` | **no** | yes | **no entry** | orphan file |

Two things do not line up. First, `img/after_export.png` is referenced by the Export section but does not exist anywhere (workspace-wide search found nothing); the manifest itself admits the capture was expected and never produced. Customers would see a broken image. Second, `img/unused_capture_07.png` exists on disk (and is committed) but is referenced by nothing and has no manifest entry — it shows a "PATIENT LIST" screen. It should be removed or given a manifest entry; a stray patient-list capture sitting in the release-image folder of a clinic product is also a privacy-hygiene concern, and would leak if the email tooling bundles the whole `img/` directory.

**4. Anything else that should not appear in a message sent to customers?**

Yes, two things beyond the factual errors above:

- **The footer, line 33: "Highlights draft assembled with AI assistance."** Two problems: it announces the email is a *draft*, which must never appear in the sent version; and it is an AI-attribution artifact. I found no stated attribution policy anywhere in the clinic-portal repo, so whether any AI-assistance note belongs in customer communications is the owner's call to confirm — but a "draft … AI assistance" line in a polished customer email is clearly an internal artifact, and I would remove it pending that confirmation.
- **The "(shown with production data)" parenthetical, lines 16–17.** Beyond being false (the captures are `seed-demo`), it is the wrong thing to say to clinic customers even when true: it asserts that real patient/clinic data is being screenshotted into marketing email, which is a privacy red flag for a healthcare product. It should be removed or replaced with "shown with demo data."

- **The footer, line 33: "Highlights draft assembled with AI assistance."** Two problems: it announces the email is a *draft*, which must never appear in the sent version; and it is an AI-attribution artifact. I found no stated attribution policy anywhere in the clinic-portal repo, so whether any AI-assistance note belongs in customer communications is the owner's call to confirm — but a "draft … AI assistance" line in a polished customer email is clearly an internal artifact, and I would remove it pending that confirmation.
- **The "(shown with production data)" parenthetical, lines 16–17.** Beyond being false (the captures are `seed-demo`), it is the wrong thing to say to clinic customers even when true: it asserts that real patient/clinic data is being screenshotted into marketing email, which is a privacy red flag for a healthcare product. It should be removed or replaced with "shown with demo data."

sections.plan: The deliverable under review is `clinic-portal/docs/release/highlights-v4.md`, a customer-facing "What's new in v4" email draft for a clinic scheduling product. Because it is customer-facing, I planned a full verification pass rather than a skim: build a fact sheet of every claim in the document, then check each claim against the only authoritative sources available in this repo — the application code, the capture manifest (`captures.json`), the image files themselves, and git history. For the screenshots specifically, I planned the integrity checks appropriate to before/after documents: confirm every referenced image exists, confirm every existing image is referenced, and open each before/after pair to confirm both sides show the same surface in a comparable state.
